semantics: Dates are ISO days; durations and lags are working days on the case calendar (workdays: ISO 1=Mon..7=Sun; exceptions: day -> is_workday).
Tasks are listed in outline order (sort = index). parent = key of the phase row. A phase is a task with a non-cancelled child.
Phases and CANCELLED tasks are not in the network; links touching them are ignored (ignored_links).
Integer boundaries: ordinal 0 = first working day on/after the anchor; a task occupies es..ef-1 (ef = es + duration); duration 0 = point.
FS es(s) >= ef(p)+lag; SS es(s) >= es(p)+lag; FF ef(s) >= ef(p)+lag; SF ef(s) >= es(p)+lag. Unstarted tasks: es >= anchor and >= status_date.
SNET raises the start; MSO sets it (conflict when logic needs later) and pins late = early; FNLT caps late finish (conflict when early finish is later).
Actual start/finish pin a task; with an actual finish late = early. In progress + status_date: ef >= status_date + max(1, ceil(duration*(1-pct))).
A point with predecessors is a finish milestone: shown on the working day before its boundary (never before the anchor); without, on the boundary day.
Backward pass from PF = max ef: total_float = lf - ef, free_float = min(link slack | PF - ef when no successor, total_float). Critical = total_float <= 0 and not done.

start_on/due_on = actual dates when present, else early dates. Phases roll up: min start / max due, min/max early & late, min floats, any critical/conflict, duration-weighted pct (4 places), status rollup.
